description: CIS GitHub Benchmark rules for Enterprise, Organization, and Repository levels

rules.name: Enterprise SSO/SAML configured
rules.description: SAML single sign-on should be configured at the enterprise level to enforce centralized identity management and ensure all members authenticate through a trusted identity provider.
rules.remediation: Go to Enterprise Settings > Authentication security > SAML single sign-on > Enable SAML authentication.

rules.name: Enterprise audit log streaming enabled
rules.description: Audit log streaming should be enabled to ensure all audit events are forwarded to an external SIEM or log management system for retention and analysis.
rules.remediation: Go to Enterprise Settings > Audit log > Log streaming > Set up a stream to your SIEM provider.

rules.name: IP allow list configured
rules.description: An IP allow list should be configured at the enterprise level to restrict access to known trusted IP ranges and prevent unauthorized access from unknown networks.
rules.remediation: Go to Enterprise Settings > Authentication security > IP allow list > Enable and add trusted IP ranges.

rules.name: GitHub Advanced Security enabled
rules.description: GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) should be enabled at the enterprise level to provide code scanning, secret scanning, and dependency review capabilities across all organizations.
rules.remediation: Go to Enterprise Settings > Code security and analysis > GitHub Advanced Security > Enable for all organizations.

rules.name: Enterprise member privileges restricted
rules.description: Enterprise member default permissions should be restricted to prevent members from creating public repositories or having excessive default access.
rules.remediation: Go to Enterprise Settings > Policies > Repositories > Restrict repository creation and visibility defaults.

rules.name: Two-factor authentication required for all organization members
rules.description: Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds an extra layer of security beyond passwords. All organization members should be required to enable 2FA to protect against credential compromise.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Authentication security > Require two-factor authentication for everyone in the organization.

rules.name: Member repository creation restricted
rules.description: Organization members should not be able to create repositories without oversight. Restricting repository creation to administrators ensures proper governance and naming conventions.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Member privileges > Repository creation > Disable member repository creation or limit to private only.

rules.name: Default repository permission is none or read
rules.description: The default repository permission for organization members should be set to 'none' or 'read' to enforce the principle of least privilege. Members should be granted access explicitly per repository.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Member privileges > Base permissions > Set to 'No permission' or 'Read'.

rules.name: Admins cannot bypass branch protection
rules.description: Even organization and repository administrators should not be able to bypass branch protection rules. This ensures that all changes follow the same review and approval process.
rules.remediation: Enforce branch protection rules at the organization level via rulesets that include administrators.

rules.name: Repository forking policy restricted
rules.description: Repository forking should be restricted or disabled to prevent code from being duplicated outside of organizational control, reducing the risk of code leakage.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Member privileges > Repository forking > Disable forking of private repositories.

rules.name: Outside collaborators policy enforced
rules.description: Outside collaborators should require admin approval and be regularly reviewed. Uncontrolled outside collaborator access increases the attack surface.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Member privileges > Outside collaborators > Restrict invitations to organization owners only.

rules.name: GitHub Pages creation restricted
rules.description: GitHub Pages should be restricted to prevent members from inadvertently publishing sensitive content or internal documentation to public-facing Pages sites.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Member privileges > Pages creation > Restrict or disable Pages creation.

rules.name: Package publishing permissions restricted
rules.description: Package publishing should be restricted to prevent unauthorized members from publishing packages that could introduce supply chain risks.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Member privileges > Package creation > Restrict public package creation.

rules.name: Security advisories enabled
rules.description: Private vulnerability reporting and security advisories should be enabled at the organization level to allow responsible disclosure and coordinated vulnerability management.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Code security and analysis > Enable private vulnerability reporting.

rules.name: Dependency graph enabled for organization
rules.description: The dependency graph should be enabled for all repositories in the organization to provide visibility into dependencies and identify potential supply chain vulnerabilities.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Code security and analysis > Dependency graph > Enable for all repositories.

rules.name: Dependabot alerts enabled for organization
rules.description: Dependabot alerts should be enabled at the organization level to automatically notify repository maintainers about known vulnerabilities in their dependencies.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Code security and analysis > Dependabot alerts > Enable for all repositories.

rules.name: Dependabot security updates enabled for organization
rules.description: Dependabot security updates should be enabled to automatically create pull requests that update vulnerable dependencies to the minimum patched version.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Code security and analysis > Dependabot security updates > Enable for all repositories.

rules.name: Secret scanning enabled for organization
rules.description: Secret scanning should be enabled at the organization level to automatically detect tokens, keys, and other secrets that have been accidentally committed to repositories.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Code security and analysis > Secret scanning > Enable for all repositories.

rules.name: Code scanning default setup enabled
rules.description: Code scanning with CodeQL default setup should be enabled at the organization level to automatically analyze code for security vulnerabilities and coding errors.
rules.remediation: Go to Organization Settings > Code security and analysis > Code scanning > Enable default setup for all repositories.

rules.name: Branch protection enabled on default branch
rules.description: The default branch should have branch protection rules enabled to prevent direct pushes, require reviews, and enforce status checks before merging.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Add branch protection rule for the default branch.

rules.name: Pull request reviews required with minimum 1 reviewer
rules.description: At least one pull request review should be required before merging to ensure code quality and catch potential security issues through peer review.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Require pull request reviews before merging > Set required approving reviews to at least 1.

rules.name: Stale pull request reviews dismissed
rules.description: Stale pull request reviews should be automatically dismissed when new commits are pushed to ensure that reviewers re-examine any code changes made after their approval.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed.

rules.name: Status checks required before merging
rules.description: Status checks (CI/CD tests, linting, security scans) should be required to pass before a pull request can be merged to prevent broken or vulnerable code from reaching the default branch.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Require status checks to pass before merging > Add required checks.

rules.name: Signed commits required
rules.description: Signed commits should be required to verify the identity of committers and ensure that commits are authentic and have not been tampered with.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Require signed commits.

rules.name: Force pushes disabled on protected branches
rules.description: Force pushes should be disabled on protected branches to prevent history rewriting that could hide malicious changes or destroy audit trails.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Uncheck 'Allow force pushes'.

rules.name: Branch deletion disabled on protected branches
rules.description: Deletion of protected branches should be disabled to prevent accidental or malicious removal of important branches and their history.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Uncheck 'Allow deletions'.

rules.name: Conversation resolution required before merging
rules.description: All review conversations should be resolved before a pull request can be merged to ensure that all feedback and concerns have been addressed.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Branches > Branch protection > Require conversation resolution before merging.

rules.name: Secret scanning enabled on repository
rules.description: Secret scanning should be enabled on the repository to detect accidentally committed credentials, API keys, tokens, and other sensitive information.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Code security and analysis > Secret scanning > Enable.

rules.name: Push protection enabled on repository
rules.description: Push protection should be enabled to block pushes that contain secrets before they are committed to the repository, preventing secret exposure at the source.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Code security and analysis > Push protection > Enable.

rules.name: Code scanning alerts addressed
rules.description: All open code scanning alerts should be reviewed and addressed. Unresolved alerts may indicate security vulnerabilities in the codebase.
rules.remediation: Review and resolve all open code scanning alerts in the Security tab > Code scanning alerts.

rules.name: Dependabot alerts addressed
rules.description: All open Dependabot alerts should be reviewed and resolved. Unresolved alerts indicate known vulnerabilities in project dependencies.
rules.remediation: Review and resolve all open Dependabot alerts in the Security tab > Dependabot alerts.

rules.name: .gitignore file exists and is not empty
rules.description: A .gitignore file should exist and contain rules to prevent sensitive files, build artifacts, and environment-specific files from being committed.
rules.remediation: Create a .gitignore file appropriate for the project's language and framework. Use github.com/github/gitignore for templates.

rules.name: LICENSE file exists
rules.description: A LICENSE file should exist in the repository to clearly define the terms under which the code can be used, modified, and distributed.
rules.remediation: Add a LICENSE file to the repository root. Choose an appropriate license at choosealicense.com.

rules.name: README file exists
rules.description: A README file should exist to provide documentation about the project, including setup instructions, usage, and contribution guidelines.
rules.remediation: Add a README.md file to the repository root with project documentation.

rules.name: CODEOWNERS file exists
rules.description: A CODEOWNERS file should exist to define code ownership and automatically request reviews from the appropriate teams or individuals when changes are made to specific paths.
rules.remediation: Create a CODEOWNERS file in the repository root, .github/, or docs/ directory.

rules.name: No active secret scanning alerts
rules.description: There should be no active secret scanning alerts indicating exposed secrets in the repository. All detected secrets should be rotated and the alerts resolved.
rules.remediation: Rotate all exposed secrets immediately, then dismiss resolved alerts in Security tab > Secret scanning alerts.

rules.name: GitHub Actions restricted to approved actions
rules.description: GitHub Actions should be restricted to only allow approved actions from verified creators or specific repositories to prevent execution of untrusted third-party code.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Actions > General > Actions permissions > Allow select actions and reusable workflows.

rules.name: GITHUB_TOKEN permissions restricted to read
rules.description: The default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions should be set to read-only. Workflows should explicitly request write permissions only when needed, following the principle of least privilege.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions > Set to 'Read repository contents and packages permissions'.

rules.name: Workflow approvals required for fork pull requests
rules.description: Workflow runs from fork pull requests should require approval from maintainers to prevent unauthorized code execution via malicious pull requests from forks.
rules.remediation: Go to Repository Settings > Actions > General > Fork pull request workflows > Require approval for all outside collaborators.
